correctness.rationale: For fixed positive \(\mu,D,r\) and \(N\ge3\), the common Poisson age \(A\sim\operatorname{Exp}(r)\) makes \(S=e^{-2\mu A}\) exactly \(\operatorname{Beta}(\beta,1)\), with \(\beta=r/(2\mu)\). Conditioned on \(S\), the maximum is \(\sqrt{D/\mu}\sqrt{1-S}\) times the maximum of \(N\) independent standard normals. The exact beta-weighted Gaussian-maximum integral has density \(\beta(\log N)^{-\beta}v^{\beta-1}\). Normal-tail Mills ratios and Gaussian extreme-value normalization give the Gumbel exceedance function \(1-\exp(-e^{-x-v})\) pointwise; an explicit integrable envelope \(v^{\beta-1}e^{-v/4}\) away from a fixed cutoff permits dominated convergence. Conditional age selection follows by bounded test functions and continuous mapping; the nominal uncorrected edge has extra Gaussian-tail factor \(1/\sqrt{4\pi\log N}\), giving amplitude \(\Gamma(\beta+1)/\sqrt{4\pi}\). The proof covers every fixed real \(x\) and \(\beta>0\). It does not claim changing-coordinate uniformity or finite-N error rates. A standalone numerical checker passed 94 diagnostics but is not offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original model publication identifies a slow 1/log N edge cutoff but does not quantify how often the nominal compact edge is exceeded, by what amplitude, or what reset ages select such events. The new exact K_beta(x) and Gamma(beta+1)/sqrt(4pi) constants separate Gaussian quantile correction from reset-age endpoint suppression, reveal a different exponent beta+1/2 for the natural uncorrected threshold, and give a conditional rare-environment distribution rather than just one-point extrema. This is a mathematically motivated next-order extreme-event characterization in a correlated gas, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a generic restatement of standard Gumbel convergence. Scientific use is bounded to the specified stationary harmonic common-reset model; no experimental prediction is asserted.
